votes.reasoning: This is a re-vote on the reworked tracker. When a failure finds status .denied, it sets authorizationKnownDenied and parks the crossing instead of un-marking it (NotificationService.swift:195-199). Later failures while the denial is cached park the crossing without asking the OS (line 190). A denied app therefore makes no more add() calls and writes no more error lines per tick. What remains is at most one settings query per observe of a vendor that has a parked crossing, with no log. A transient failure while authorized still re-arms (line 201). The 4 tests pass. Reversal to HEAD turned all 4 RED (count 2 == 1, statusQueries 0 == 1, 0 == 2); restored after. Everything runs on the MainActor: the class is @MainActor, the completion is @MainActor @Sendable, and SystemNotificationCenter hops through Task { @MainActor }.

deliveryFinished (NotificationService.swift:183-205) is about 22 lines. It has 2 guards, and the closure holds 1 if, so nesting is 2. The error is still logged at .error before any branch, so nothing is swallowed. The Error is turned into a String before the Task hop, which keeps the closure Sendable. With a cached denial, a failure now parks the crossing (tracker.park) instead of leaving it marked for good, and the denial is cleared both on success and on re-check. The doc comment on the property (:62-66) names both finding ids. hasParked (:310) scans every key, but it only runs while authorizationKnownDenied is true, and the key count is tiny (vendors x windows), so it is not a hot-path concern.

Once a denial is known, a failure still parks the crossing with no retry (deliveryFinished at :190). The only new OS call is the gated re-check covered under BUG-MAE-013, which does not add() or log, so the PERF goal holds. No new dependency, host, entitlement or file is added.
